answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the cipher schedule in the timber ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the atlas checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 165 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 23 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
